ALTHOUGH THE REASON FOR IGNITION IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION, TECH DISPATCH DETECTED 0.5% METHANE AT THE MANHOLE AND GAS CREW DISPATCH DETECTED 97% METHANE IN THE MANHOLE ELECTRIC DUCT. READINGS ALL CLEAR AT OTHER LOCATIONS. 3 PEOPLE HOSPITALIZED, 1 HELD OVER NIGHT FOR OBSERVATION, 2 RELEASED.

properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 809999

Nearest City: Fairbanks, AK
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: #1 ARCTIC GRADE DIESEL FUEL
Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party: ALASKA VILLAGE ELECTRIC COOP.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 54 gallons
///WEB REPORT/// AFTER DAYTANK FILLING OPERATIONS (LOGGED AT 9:10 PM 8/30/06) THE PLANT OPERATOR DID NOT VALVE OFF THE LINE FROM THE BULK TANK TO THE DAYTANK. HEAD PRESSURE FROM THE BULK TANK OVER FILLED THE DAYTANK AND FORCED FUEL THROUGH POORLY SEALED THREADS AROUND THE TANK GUAGE AT THE TOP OF THE TANK. #1 ARCTIC GRADE FUEL OIL SEEPED THROUGH THE THREADS, RAN DOWN THE TANK ONTO THE CONCRETE FLOOR AND SPREAD OUT AGAINST THE WALL OF THE METAL BUILDING. FUEL SEEPED UNDER THE WALL AND INTO THE SOIL ALONG THE BUILDING FOUNDATION. WE HAVE RECOVERED (4) 55 GALLON DRUMS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL AND ARE STILL DIGGING DOWN IN GRAVELY SOIL. THE LIMITS OF THE TRENCH ARE 20 FEET LONG, 10" WIDE AND 2 FEET DEEP. AN ESTIMATE OF FUEL LOST HAS NOT BEEN DETERMINED BUT IS EXPECTED TO BE LESS THAN 55 GALLONS.

properties.content:

Location2: INDUSTRIAL FACILITY

Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: CC 1 INDUSTRY, LLC
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 18.175559, -66.161315 (Approximated from route)
Reported Spill Volume: 5500 gallon
Report DescriptionCALLER STATED THAT THE EMERGENCY GENERATOR FUEL DAY TANKS ARE BEING FILLED UP WITH DIESEL FUEL USING TWO FUEL PUMPS. BEFORE THE TANK WAS FULL THE OPERATOR SWITCHED OFF 1 PUMP, AND FORGOT TO SWITCH OFF THE OTHER PUMP. THE TANK FILLED UP AND OVERFLOWED ALL THE WAY TO THE ROOF VENT. AND APPROX. AMOUNT OF 5500 GALLONS OF DIESEL FUEL OIL WENT INTO THE ROOF AND INTO THE SECONDARY CONTAINMENT BASIN. THE SPILLED FUEL OIL WAS RECOVERED. AND CLEANED UP. LATER, THE NEIGHBORHOOD COMPLAINED OF PETROLEUM ODOR COMING FROM A NEARBY CREEK, AND POSSIBLY SOME THE FUEL OIL SPILLED FROM THE ROOF, WENT INTO THE ROOFING JOINT SYSTEM, AND POURED TO A STORM DRAIN SYSTEM , AND INTO A SMALL NEARBY CREEK DUE TO RAIN. LOCAL DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES WAS CALLED IN. AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF FUEL OIL MAY HAVE SPILLED TO THE CREEK.
